Prevention: Plant in new field using disease free cassava stems
Plant resistant cassava varieties such as
Remove and destroy all volunteer cassava plants in the field before planting
Don’t move cassava planting materials from affected areas
Avoid planting alternate hosts of the white fly ( Bemisia tabaci ) near the cassava fields
Monitoring: Inspect the cassava field every week for infected plants
Inspect the field for vectors (white flies).
Look on the underside of leaves for white flies.
Inspect during morning hours before 11 am.
Inspect during evening hours after 4 pm.
Whiteflies tend to hide when temperatures are high
Look for reduced leaf size, malformed and twisted leaves, with yellow areas separated by areas of normal green colour.
Direct Control: Uproot and destroy infected cassava plants
Diseased plant materials can be fed to animals.
Early planting, at the beginning of the rains.
Restrictions: Chemical products are available against the white flies but due to their high mobility, it is not useful to spray.
